apple.treatment_profile: Often coated with food-grade wax (shellac or carnauba) to retain moisture and add shine. Possible pesticide residue on skin.
apple.recommendation: Wash under running water for 20-30 seconds; a brief baking-soda rinse helps remove surface residue.

tomato.treatment_profile: Tomatoes may be harvested mature-green and exposed to controlled ethylene to synchronize ripening. Food-grade coatings can reduce moisture loss during transport.
tomato.recommendation: Wash under running water before cutting; keep uncut tomatoes at room temperature until ripe and refrigerate only after cutting.

potato.treatment_profile: Commercial potatoes may receive approved sprout-inhibitor treatments during storage. Green skin indicates light exposure and possible elevated glycoalkaloids.
potato.recommendation: Store in a cool, dry, dark, ventilated place; discard potatoes with extensive greening, bitter taste, or advanced decay.

banana.treatment_profile: Bananas are commonly harvested green and may be ripened in controlled ethylene rooms. The peel is a natural barrier and is not normally wax-coated.
banana.recommendation: Keep unripe bananas at room temperature; separate ripe fruit from other produce to slow or control ethylene-driven ripening.

carrot.treatment_profile: Carrots are commonly washed and chilled after harvest. Surface moisture and damaged tissue increase the risk of soft rot during storage.
carrot.recommendation: Remove leafy tops, refrigerate in a ventilated container, and wash thoroughly under running water before eating.
